description:
On Linux (release profile, per the workspace hard rule), "cargo test --release -p kopi-beans" gives 984 passed / 10 failed / 4 ignored. The 10 are stable across 6 consecutive full runs, and are NOT caused by any local change -- verified by stashing the working tree and running the same 6 times.

Stable failures:
  core::tombstone::tests::test_join_different_id_panics (should panic, did not)
  core::tombstone::tests::test_join_different_lineage_panics (should panic, did not)
  daemon::runtime::core::tests::restores_hlc_state_for_non_daemon_actor
  daemon::runtime::executor::tests::mutation_allocates_dot_counter_in_wal_index_without_rewriting_store_meta
  daemon::runtime::executor::tests::mutation_atomic_commit_failpoint_rolls_back_event_and_watermark
  daemon::runtime::store::runtime::tests::bootstrap_crash_before_meta_commit_recovers_on_next_open
  daemon::runtime::store::runtime::tests::phase3_head_sha_loads_from_index
  daemon::runtime::store::runtime::tests::runtime_upgrades_stale_index_meta_and_rebuilds_legacy_index
  daemon::runtime::store::runtime::tests::stale_pending_marker_does_not_rollback_later_committed_meta
  git::sync::tests::migrate_store_ref_to_v2_dry_run_peeks_remote_without_mutating_tracking_ref

Plus one order-dependent flake: daemon::runtime::executor::tests::mutation_span_includes_realtime_context failed 1/6 baseline runs and 2/6 after an unrelated change, but passes 5/5 alone. gh-18 already noted this class in passing ("the release-mode failure count varied between 10, 11 and 12") and said it was never filed separately. This is that filing.

KEY FINDING -- the first two are gh-18, which is CLOSED as completed (2026-08-13), and they still fail here. Checked why: published kopi-beans 0.1.7 promoted those invariants to hard assert_eq! with a rustdoc note telling the reader not to put debug_assert_eq! back. Repo HEAD (crates/kopi-beans/src/core/tombstone.rs:60-61) still has debug_assert_eq!. So the gh-18 fix exists only in the published crate and was never committed here.

That makes this bead partly EVIDENCE FOR bd-s06 / gh-71 rather than ten independent bugs: GitHub issues are being closed against work that never landed in git. Some unknown number of the remaining 8 may likewise already be fixed in the 0.1.7 tree.

So: reconcile bd-s06 FIRST, re-run the suite against the reconciled tree, and only then triage whatever is still red. Debugging these against in-tree code risks re-fixing what is already fixed.

Shape of what is left, if it survives reconciliation: 7 of the 8 cluster in store/WAL/meta (watermarks, index meta, bootstrap recovery) -- e.g. phase3_head_sha_loads_from_index panics at store/runtime.rs:2234 on .expect("applied watermark"), an Option that was None. A shared root cause is plausible.

Why it matters: a suite red by default cannot act as a gate. Any real regression from here on is invisible against a 10-failure background -- this session needed 12 full suite runs just to prove one change added nothing new.
title: kopi-beans: 10 stable test failures + 1 flake on Linux, suite is red by default

description:
GH: https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam/issues/9
Part of the CJK / annotated-PDF field report (2026-08-01), epic bd-ski.
Original write-up: docs/issues/field-report-2026-08-01/

--- original GH body, verbatim ---


> Part of the **pdf2md CJK/annotated-PDF** work order — see the tracking issue for shared context, the corrections in §0, and the additive-corruption principle these cards rest on.

**Confidence:** High. **Owns:** `kopitiam_skill.md`. **Land first — docs only, no code.**

## Problem

The skill doc instructs agents:

> Read the validation / recovery report: `pdf2md` prints a report comparing the extracted word count against the rendered Markdown word count, ending in a PASS/FAIL line.

Two problems:

1. It says **word** count — stale since `kopitiam-wwr`; it is non-whitespace character count now (`validation/mod.rs:189`).
2. It implies PASS means the output is good.

**Agents follow this literally.** I did: I read `Status: PASS` on five documents, trusted it, and used corrupted output downstream.

## Change

State what PASS does and does not mean:

> **PASS means no content was lost. It does not mean the output is correct.**

Name the classes it cannot see — duplication, character substitution, displacement (see tracking issue §1) — and advise a visual check for CJK or annotation-heavy documents. Fix "word count" → "non-whitespace character count". Once F-1/F-2 land, add the new warnings to the same paragraph.

## Acceptance

- [ ] An agent reading only the skill doc would not conclude PASS means the output is trustworthy.

Cheapest fix on the list. Do it first — it stops the next agent repeating my mistake while the code cards are still in survey.

---

Tracking: #2
title: [docs] F-6 — kopitiam_skill.md overstates what a PASS report means
